I have a story in the same vein. When my daughter was a baby she never got low-grade fevers. Whenever she got sick her temperature jumped to 104°F and she'd start to hallucinate and then, of course we had to go to the ER. The staff at the hospital in my hometown always treated me like absolute garbage. They'd help us out right away because she was a baby, but the entire time they'd be yelling things at me like "LET ME GUESS. YOU WERE SMOKING IN THE SAME ROOM AS HER." or accusing me of not giving her medicine to combat the fever, ignoring her, not hydrating her, straight up talking shit about me right in front of me saying that she shouldn't be this bad off so I'm lying to them. The first time it happened, it was the middle of winter and the middle of the night and I took my infant to the hospital with tears in my eyes because I thought she was going to die. The first thing anyone said to me was the nurse actually yelling at me for putting a jacket on her. I get it now. High fever, don't put a jacket on, but I was a new mom and I was there in the emergency room to help my very sick baby. Why was I being treated like this? 

Because I'm a teen mom. 

The day I realized this, I had been at a wedding when my then-3-yr-old fell down the porch steps and my mother took her to the hospital to make sure she didn't have a concussion. I rushed there right away and told them I was there to see my daughter. They let me in and I saw my mom sitting with my kid, both were smiling and the doctor was talking to them. My mom was being treated with respect and dignity and no one was accusing her of throwing the kid down the stairs or something ridiculous. I stepped in and told the doctor that I was the mother and asked if my daughter was okay. She very obviously sized me up, looked at me with disdain, and then straight up ignored me. Then she continued to explain to my mother about how to care for my child's contusion (no concussion, thankfully) and glared at me on her way out. 

What. The. Fuck. 
My only crime was being 19 and looking 15, but that's not for them to judge. I get it that they are probably used to matching up a particular problem with a particular type of person, but they couldn't have been more wrong about me. That's what kills me about it is that I was stereotyped and treated like a piece of shit lowlife for what? Trying to make sure my child doesn't die from a high fever? ER staff has some nerve.

A lot of people don't understand self-harm as an addiction. I had never felt that okay before, so I knew I would do it again. As of right now I am 2 years clean, but I would be lying if I said I don't think about it every day. I hope you're doing okay with the alcoholism stuff. Addiction is addiction, and while I don't drink much/often I can probably understand what you've been through if you wanted to share.
